user_stories.story: As the maintainer, I run `python data/validate.py` (no DB, no network, from repo root) and get a clear per-problem failure message and non-zero exit when routes.geojson breaks any SPEC 9.3 rule, so bad data never reaches CI-green.

As the maintainer, I run `python -m data.seed` (or via docker compose run --rm api) and the route, stop and route_stop tables are replaced atomically from routes.geojson without touching reports; I can re-run it any time.
As a contributor, I read data/README.md and learn provenance, the pin table, the OSM/ODbL credit, how to re-snap, and the known gaps.
As a reader, SPEC.md, CLAUDE.md, README.md and docs/* all agree with the code (9 route records, seed available, validate real).

files.file: app/queries.py (add the seed SQL function; SQL stays out of data/seed.py per hard rule 2)
tests/data/__init__.py, tests/data/test_validate.py, tests/data/test_seed.py (plus a small fixture helper that builds a valid in-memory FeatureCollection and writes variants to tmp_path)
.github/workflows/ci.yml (validate step real; no OSRM, no DB needed by it)
SPEC.md, CLAUDE.md (Commands block), README.md, docs/ARCHITECTURE.md, docs/DECISIONS.md, docs/OPEN_ITEMS.md, docs/roadmap.md

acceptance_criteria.criterion: `python data/validate.py` run from repo root (also `python -m data.validate`) against the committed data/routes/routes.geojson exits 0 with a short summary (route count, stop count, warnings), with no DB and no network. The CI step `python data/validate.py` works as written (script invocation must be able to import app.config for SERVICE_BBOX).

validate accepts an optional path argument to the geojson file (default data/routes/routes.geojson) so tests can feed variants. Each failure prints one line per problem naming the route_id (and seq/stop_id where relevant) and the exit code is non-zero (1). All problems are collected and reported together, not just the first.

File-level failures, each non-zero exit with a clear message and no traceback: file missing; empty file; not valid JSON; top-level not a FeatureCollection with a `features` list; a feature whose geometry type is not LineString; a LineString with fewer than 2 coordinates; zero features.

Bbox: any line coordinate or stop lat/lng outside SERVICE_BBOX fails. Bbox is read via app.config (load_settings / env SERVICE_BBOX), order lat_min,lat_max,lng_min,lng_max, not hardcoded. Test with a point that is in-box only if lat/lng are not swapped, so a [lat,lng] mix-up on the line (GeoJSON is [lng,lat]) is caught.
Non-numeric, null, NaN, Infinity, bool or missing coordinates (in line points or stop lat/lng) fail with a message, not a crash.

Stop seq: stops are checked in list order as seq 1..n (the geojson stops array has no explicit seq; seq is the 1-based index). A gap/"not starting at 1" failure applies where an explicit `seq` is present on stop objects; if absent, order index is used. Tests must cover seq gap and seq not starting at 1 using an explicit `seq` key on stop objects (validate tolerates and checks an optional `seq`; seed ignores it and uses list order). See decisions D1.
A route with fewer than 2 stops fails.

Registry: route_id must match {color}_{direction}, split on the LAST underscore; color must be one of the six, direction out/back. All 9 registry IDs must be present (a missing one fails and is named). yellow_back, purple_back, grey_back fail; any unknown route_id (e.g. "orange_out", "nounderscore") fails. properties.color/direction must equal the values derived from route_id, and name must equal the registry name for the color.

Missing any SPEC 9.1 property (route_id, color, direction, name, source, verified_on, osm_relation_id, stops; and per stop: stop_id, name, lat, lng, osm_node_id) fails naming the property. Present-with-null is fine for verified_on, osm_relation_id, osm_node_id. `source` must be "memory-traced" (fail otherwise); osm_relation_id/osm_node_id must be null. Empty/non-string stop_id or name fails.
Two features sharing a route_id fails (duplicate route_id).

Same stop_id on two different routes with coordinates more than 100 m apart fails (haversine). The real 55 m Pampang case (yellow_out vs blue_out/blue_back) and the 26 m Red Terminal case pass. Exactly 100 m is a pass (strictly greater fails).
Line gap: any consecutive pair of line points more than 50 m apart fails, naming route_id and the index. Exactly 50 m passes.

Stop-to-line: a stop more than 100 m from the nearest point of its own route line fails, naming route_id and stop_id. Distance is to the nearest densified line point (vertex), as the line is densified to at most 40 m; no segment projection required. A stop exactly 100 m away passes.

Warning (exit stays 0): two DIFFERENT stop_ids (across the whole file, including within one route) whose coordinates are closer than 30 m print a line starting with "WARNING". The same stop_id appearing twice on one route (circular return pass) or on several routes produces no warning and no failure. Warnings never change the exit code, but if there is also a failure the warnings are still printed.
Circular routes: a stop_id repeated at two positions on one route is valid for validate (no duplicate-stop failure, no seq error). Both occurrences are checked for stop-to-line distance.
Passing-file test: a minimal valid FeatureCollection with all 9 registry routes exits 0. The committed routes.geojson is also asserted valid by a test (guards drift between snapshot and rules).

`python -m data.seed` loads routes.geojson (optional path arg), runs the validate checks first and refuses (non-zero, nothing written) if they fail, applies sql/schema.sql (idempotent) so it also works against an empty database, then replaces route/stop/route_stop in ONE transaction: DELETE route_stop, DELETE route, DELETE stop, INSERT stop, INSERT route, INSERT route_stop. Prints counts (routes, stops, route_stop rows). Exit 0.

Seed result against the committed file: 9 route rows; one stop row per distinct stop_id (fewer than total route_stop-linked stop entries because of shared stops); route_stop rows = sum of stops entries over all routes, with seq = 1-based list order per route. Circular routes insert the same stop_id at two seq values without error. route.line stored as jsonb [[lng,lat],...]; source, verified_on, osm_relation_id copied; stop.osm_node_id copied.

Shared stop rows: exactly one stop row per stop_id. The winning name/lat/lng is the first occurrence when features are processed in sorted route_id order and stops in list order (deterministic, independent of file order). Test: two routes with the same stop_id at different coordinates (within 100 m) yields the coordinates of the lexicographically smaller route_id.
Re-run idempotent: running seed twice leaves identical table contents (same row counts and values), no duplicate-key errors.

Report rows survive: report rows inserted before a seed (and before a re-seed) are unchanged afterwards (count and content). Seed never issues any statement on report (test may also check no report FK exists, so replacement is never blocked).

Atomic rollback: a failure mid-way (e.g. a route_stop insert violating a constraint, or an injected exception after the DELETEs) leaves the previous route/stop/route_stop data fully intact and exits non-zero with a clear log line. Test seeds good data, then seeds a file that fails during the transaction (bypassing or with validation disabled via the underlying queries function), and asserts old rows remain.

Seed with the database unreachable: no traceback; a clear one-line log message and non-zero exit. Seed with a missing/invalid geojson: clear message, non-zero exit, DB untouched. Database URL comes from DATABASE_URL via app.config (default as in config); tests point it at TEST_DATABASE_URL.

Hard rules: all seed SQL lives in app/queries.py, parameterised with %s (no string formatting of values); data/seed.py contains no SQL text; no new dependencies in requirements.txt; no ORM; planner untouched. Seed uses the existing app.db pool (init_pool / close_pool), with pool closed on exit.

Existing test suite still passes; new tests under tests/data/ pass with `pytest` against the Postgres test DB. Test fixtures for seed clean route/stop/route_stop before/after (without breaking the autouse clean_reports fixture) and do not leave seed data that breaks other tests. validate tests need no DB.

data/README.md exists and contains: provenance table (snap date 2026-10-25; each of the 9 route records with source "memory-traced", not ridden/unverified, listed as known gaps); the pin table copied from docs/OPEN_ITEMS.md, with README as the single source (OPEN_ITEMS links to it instead of duplicating); the credit "(c) OpenStreetMap contributors" and an ODbL/OSM copyright link, stating line geometry comes from OSRM on OSM road data and stop positions are hand-placed; how to re-snap (waypoints.csv edit, snap_routes.py, validate, seed, including --dry-run/--reuse); known gaps: Checkpoint/Highway not named stops, Jurio Foodhouse placeholder pin (15.1680300,120.5835400), blue out/back direction vs SPEC registry unresolved.

Anti-drift greps return nothing stale across *.md, ci.yml: "12 routes"/"12 route records", "Day 1 stub", "not yet available", "seed: Day 2". CLAUDE.md Commands block shows `docker compose run --rm api python -m data.seed` as available and validate as real (not stub, exits non-zero on failure). SPEC Section 9.2/9.3 describes validate additions actually implemented (30 m warning, source/null checks, optional-seq handling, seed runs validation first, schema applied by seed, tie-break rule for shared stops, circular route handling); SPEC and code agree on every rule and threshold. docs/DECISIONS.md has entries (what / why / rejected alternative, 3 lines) for snap densify+join check, validate, seed. docs/ARCHITECTURE.md pipeline section matches. roadmap and OPEN_ITEMS mark Day 2 Track A items done/open accurately. README.md has the seed command and mentions validate.
CI: ci.yml runs `python data/validate.py` as a real step (after checkout/install, no OSRM, no network beyond pip); a failing validation fails the job. Test step order unchanged.

decisions.decision: The geojson stop objects carry no seq in SPEC 9.1; seq = 1-based list index and cannot gap in a file produced by snap_routes. The request still requires gap and "not starting at 1" tests. Resolution: validate also validates waypoints.csv-independent data only, so it accepts an OPTIONAL integer `seq` on each stop object; when present it must equal 1..n in order (gap, duplicate, or not starting at 1 fails); when absent, list index is used. SPEC 9.1 notes that `seq` is optional and ignored by seed. (Alternative if implementer prefers: validate data/raw/waypoints.csv seq too; either way the tests must exercise both failure kinds. Do not change snap_routes output.)

Seed SQL lives in app/queries.py as one function taking the parsed features (plain data) and doing everything in one db.connection() block (commit on success, rollback on exception). data/seed.py only parses, validates, calls it, and reports.
Shared stop coordinates: first occurrence by sorted route_id then list order wins. Documented in SPEC 9.3, data/README.md and DECISIONS.
report has no FK to route or stop in sql/schema.sql, so DELETE/INSERT replacement is never blocked; if a future FK is added it must not block replacement (note in DECISIONS).

Seed validates first and applies the idempotent schema itself (the api container may not have started yet). The validation logic is shared by importing it from data/validate.py; no duplicate rule implementation.
Line-to-stop and join distances use haversine to the nearest densified line point (matches snap_routes.dist_m and check_joins); no segment projection.
Blue out/back direction vs registry (Pandan to Pampang): left as is, recorded as known gap in data/README.md and OPEN_ITEMS. Not blocking.

assumptions.assumption: The committed routes.geojson (snapped 2026-10-25) passes all validate rules; if it does not, that is a data finding to report, not to hide by loosening a threshold or editing snap output.
Thresholds (100 m, 50 m, 30 m) are fixed by SPEC 9.3 and are module constants in validate.py, not env tunables (SPEC Section 10 does not list them); SERVICE_BBOX is the only config read.
The Docker image already copies data/ (Dockerfile COPY data ./data), so `docker compose run --rm api python -m data.seed` works without Dockerfile changes; Dockerfile pins stay as-is.
Nothing is committed or pushed; OSRM is not called.

edge_cases.case: Stop lat/lng keys vs GeoJSON [lng,lat] order: swapped order must be caught by bbox.
route_id "darkyellow_out" splits to darkyellow/out; ids with no underscore or extra underscores ("dark_yellow_out") fail as unknown.
Circular route repeating a stop_id: not a duplicate for validate, seed or the near-duplicate warning.
Two different stop_ids under 30 m (including Jurio Foodhouse placeholder neighbours) only warn.
Boundary values exactly 100/50/30 m behave as stated (30 m: warn only if strictly less).
Features with a stops list that is missing or not a list; properties not an object; feature with null geometry.
validate run from a different cwd or as a script must still import app.config and find the default file path relative to the module, not cwd.
Seed against a DB where tables are empty, already populated, or missing (schema applied).
Seed interrupted mid-transaction leaves old data; reports untouched throughout.
Unicode in stop names (non-ASCII) and apostrophes round-trip through seed via parameters.

risks.risk: Committed routes.geojson might fail a rule (for example a stop over 100 m from its line or a 30 m near-duplicate pair); the fix is data/waypoint work, not threshold changes. Report the findings.
validate.py invoked as a script puts data/ (not repo root) on sys.path, so importing app.config can fail in CI; needs explicit handling and a test that runs it as a subprocess from the repo root.
Seed tests share the Postgres test DB with API tests; leftover route data or table drops could break other tests. Fixtures must isolate and clean up.
Doc drift across seven files; the anti-drift grep list may miss phrasing variants.
Jurio Foodhouse placeholder pin and unresolved blue direction mean seeded data is knowingly imperfect; documented as known gaps.

Python stdlib only; no new packages

spec.self_critique: Every user story maps to criteria: validate (1-16, 28), seed (17-25), README (26), anti-drift (27). All criteria are observable by exit code, output line, or table contents. Biggest remaining risks: D1 (the seq rule is awkward because the geojson format has no seq, so the optional-seq reading is my interpretation of the request and SPEC) and whether the committed snapshot actually satisfies the rules. Neither is blocking: the D1 default is stated and the data-failure case is reported rather than hidden.
